title: What If You Chewed Ice Every Day?

scenes.text: What if you craved ice every single day? It might be your blood talking.
Doctors have a name for it, pagophagia. It's very common in people with iron deficiency anemia.
In twenty fourteen, a Penn psychologist tested why. Anemic and healthy volunteers took a twenty-two minute reaction test.
Without ice, the anemic group was slower and more erratic. After chewing ice, they did about as well as everyone else.
Healthy people got no boost at all. Her theory: cold in the mouth may push more blood to the brain.
So if you can't stop crunching ice, it may be worth a blood test.

What if you chewed ice every day? Craving ice, called pagophagia, is very common in people with iron deficiency anemia.
In a 2014 University of Pennsylvania study, anemic volunteers who had ice before a 22-minute reaction test performed about as well as healthy people, while healthy volunteers got no benefit. This is not medical advice: ask a doctor about cravings.
